#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  # gh-2042 (review): ONE call for the WHOLE list — the gate's contract is
  # per-call all-or-nothing ("refuse before any upload"), so per-asset
  # invocation would judge each asset against its own release-view
  # snapshot (N round-trips, a wider draft→published TOCTOU window, and a
  # partial mutation when an early benign asset uploads before a later
  # fa-* refusal).
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "${assets[@]}"
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework + gh-2042): publish + latest ONLY
  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
        # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
        bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi

release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. gh-1537: NO main-push arm — ci.yml
    # no longer triggers on pushes to main (the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired), so releases arm on the 2h coalesce schedule and the two
    # gated dispatches only. Every armed tick cuts an annotated tag
    # (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and
    # CI stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish
    # time. The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because
    # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries
    # jobs (gh-1172); the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no
    # branch push), but remains the release-path actor (gh-1402).
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true)) &&
      needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push, nothing else. gh-1801: auto_release.sh no longer
          # creates the GitHub Release (an asset-less create publishes an
          # empty `latest`) — the tag-run binaries job owns creation.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          fetch-depth: 0

          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag

          # auto_release.sh no longer calls `gh` at all (the asset-less
          # create published an empty `latest` and broke `fa update`; the
          # binaries job owns creation, draft-first). The tag push rides
          # the checkout App token above (gh-1172).
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

The attach job SUCEEDS (attaching to a draft is valid). The train guard ran at ~T+1h (train failed fast) — at that moment the build-mobile run was STILL in-flight (3h+ chain) → if build-mobile's run id was the MARKER (i.e., build-mobile's release-mobile CREATED the draft — only if no draft existed yet)...

Scenario: train fails at T+1h; guard deletes the existing draft (owner completed) ✓; THEN at T+3h build-mobile's release-mobile runs attach_or_create → release gone (deleted) → **CREATES A NEW DRAFT** (marker run = build-mobile's run) → uploads IPA → job succeeds → **a brand-new orphan draft for a dead train, created AFTER the guard** → rots 24h → swept → sweep issue re-files. ✗ THE HOLE IS REAL POST-FIX — this exact chain needs only: a tag train failing while a daily mobile leg (3h chain) is mid-flight on the same next tag. The daily legs run daily; a failed train happens whenever core tests flake on a tag push. This WILL recur.

Also the windows leg (85m chain) — same exposure. ✓ my fix (sweep-side reclaim) handles ALL of these at the next daily — the draft gets reclaimed ≤24h after creation with the train named, then the sweep goes clean → issue auto-closes. The rot window shrinks from unbounded-growth to ≤~24h AND, more importantly, each failed train produces exactly ONE sweep notification instead of the draft surviving to produce recurring ones... hmm, actually with the current code the draft also gets deleted at the first sweep past 24h (one notification). The DIFFERENCE my fix makes:
1. No 24h+ rot for provably-dead drafts (issue #282 invariant: a pipeline draft ends published or deleted — now enforced even when the creating step's publish owner died before the draft was even born).
2. The reclaim happens EVEN WHEN THE DRAFT IS FRESH — currently a fresh draft is untouched NO MATER WHAT (even provably dead). The sweep issue for v1.0.739 was only filed 44h after the failure; with the fix it's ≤~24h (next daily).
3. Crucially: the CURRENT flow for these issue filed + ">24h stale" — the RECURING issue the ticket complains about. Wait — is it actually recurring? After the sweep deletes the draft, the next sweep is clean → issue auto-closes. The recurrence the ticket text worries about ("recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing") = the DRAFT CLASS recurring (each failed train leaves another 24h rot), not the same issue staying open. My fix eliminates the class: a failed train's leftover gets reclaimed at the NEXT sweep regardless of age, with the train named once. Plus the train guard handles the at-train-end case. Between the two, every creation path for a dead-train draft is covered within one daily cycle.

OK — but honestly, let me ALSO reconsider the SIMPLER reading one more time: is the intended fix maybe just "v1.0.739 was swept pre-fix; gh-2230 already fixed it; write already_fixed.json"? The guideline flow: "Check git history, current code, and linked tests. If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop."

Is the bug genuinely fixed? The SPECIFIC swept draft (v1.0.739) is gone AND its train predated the gh-2230 fix that prevents exactly this. BUT the ticket's auto-close condition is "auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale" — sweeps keep FINDING stale drafts (11 machine drafts/day — external, plus any new dead-train drafts via the hole above). The bug CLASS is not fully fixed: the guard's one-shot semantics provably leaves the post-fix hole (my T+3h build-mobile chain). The sweep issue ITSELF says "recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing" — the sweep data shows the draft class recurring (12 swept in ONE sweep: 11 external + 1 in-repo hole). As the bug-fixing engineer I should fix the in-repo hole so the DRAFT-SWEPT issue stops recurring from OUR side, and document that the 11 machine-account drafts are external (the automation loop's own hygiene — gh-2287 handles their deletion; their creation is outside this repo).

Hmm — should I ALSO worry about making the sweep issue not re-fire for machine drafts? No — out of scope; gh-2287 made that a deliberate signal.

Let me also sanity-check the release_tag_mint.sh + verify_pubdev_release.sh story for the RCA completeness: the v1.0.739 content (commit c08bbe26) shipped later anyway? The NEXT tag v1.0.740 (cut after 07:32Z from a main containing c08bbe26 + the fix) — published via its train. So v1.0.739's CONTENT was not lost — only the intermediate tag. verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only — by the time the pubdev leg noticed v1.0.739 unserved, a newer tag existed. ✓ documented behavior, no action.

Now — write the RCA, then the RED test, then the fix.

Actually — one more design question for the fix: WHERE in the sweep loop to put the fresh-reclaim? Current loop cases: fresh / human / bot. I'll extend `fresh)`:

```bash
fresh)
 fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
 # gh-2318: a FRESH draft can still be provably never-publishable ...
 [ -n "$marker_run" ] || continue
 status probe → completed else continue
 train lookup → failed train with provenance skipped else continue
 delete + reclaimed_count++ + build issue lines
 ;;
``

And the bot branch's train-diagnosis code — extract into a function `train_diagnosis <tag>` that echoes the train_line (and sets a global for provenance-skip?). Bash functions + globals: keep it simple — write a function `lookup_train <tag>` that prints `id<TAB>conclusion<TAB>url<TAB>failed_jobs<TAB>prov_conclusion` or empty. Then both branches consume it. Careful to preserve EXACT issue prose for the gh-2105 tests.

Hmm wait — the bot branch currently runs the train lookup ONLY for stale drafts (per tag). The gh-2105 test 'fresh and human drafts never trigger a train lookup' (line 1806!) asserts fresh/human drafts cause NO train lookup. MY CHANGE BREAKS THAT TEST — deliberately: fresh MARKED drafts now trigger the lookup (only when marker present + owner completed — actually the test fixture at 1806: let me read it to see what it plants and asserts). I'll need to UPDATE that test (it pins the old behavior) — allowed: tests may be updated when behavior intentionally changes, but I must keep the SPIRIT: fresh UNMARKED drafts never trigger lookups; human drafts never do. Let me read that test.

**Bug**: The daily draft sweeper keeps filing `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issues for release drafts whose tag train failed (gh-2318: `v1.0.739`) — the draft class recurs because a failed train's staged draft can outlive the gh-2230 train-level guard and rot for 24h+ until the sweeper reclaims it.

**Root cause** — a lifecycle gap between two owners (both in-repo, evidence in the sweep entry itself):

1. **v1.0.739 (this sweep) ran the pre-fix workflow.** Tag `v1.0.739` was minted 2026-11-17T05:26:23Z by a *daily-child draft-staging leg* (`release_lazy_draft.sh` → `release_tag_mint.sh`: annotated tag `tagger github-actions[bot]`, same second as the draft's `created_at`; draft author `@IstiN` via RELEASE_PAT, ownership marker `run/402346218/job/…` — a build-macos.yml run, NOT a ci.yml run). The mint fired the tag train (ci.yml run 4024131629), which executed the ci.yml **at the tag ref** — commit `c08bbe26` (01:04Z), ancestor of the gh-2230 fix commit `cdf3467b` (07:32:36Z). That train had **no `train-draft-guard` job**; it failed upstream of the publish point (Core tests shard 3/4 → Quality gate → binaries/web-spa/build-extension skipped → `release-provenance` skipped), so the staged draft was never published, `verify_pubdev_release.sh` heals the LATEST tag only (`v1.0.740` was cut 08:44Z), and the draft rotted 44h until the daily sweeper deleted it and filed this issue.

2. **The gh-2230 guard is one-shot, so the class still recurs post-fix.** `train-draft-guard` runs exactly once, at train end. A dead-train draft can still be born or become reclaimable AFTER that moment:
   - a long daily-child leg (build-mobile TestFlight chain ≈ 3h, build-windows ≈ 85m) in flight on the same next tag calls `release_attach_or_create.sh` after the guard already ran (and/or after the guard deleted the original draft) and **creates a fresh draft** for the dead tag — its own job succeeds, so its per-job `release_draft_guard.sh` never fires;
   - the guard **keeps** a draft whose owner run was still in-flight at train end (fail-safe, correct) — but nothing ever re-examines that draft with train knowledge once the owner completes.
   In both shapes the daily sweep is the only remaining net, and `sweep_stale_drafts.sh` buckets a **fresh (<24h) draft as "untouched — an in-flight run may own them"** with no train awareness. A provably never-publishable draft (well-formed `release-draft-owner` marker, owner run completed, tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with `release-provenance` SKIPPED — `rerun --failed` cannot resurrect skipped jobs) therefore rots the full 24h+ and re-files the recurring sweep issue. That is exactly the "recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing" branch of the sweep-issue prose (issue #282 invariant: every pipeline draft ends published or deleted).

**Impact**: every failed tag train that overlaps a daily release leg leaves a staged draft rotting ≥24h; each one re-files the deduplicated `release-hygiene` issue, so the issue never stabilizes and the releases page carries unpublished draft noise for a day. (No publish content is lost: a superseded tag's commits ship with the next tag — v1.0.740…v1.0.749 cut normally.)

**Not in scope / external**: 11 of the 12 swept drafts are `ai-gh-*`/`ai-pr-*` machine-account drafts created by the @ai-teammate automation loop **outside this repo's runners** (no Actions run owns them). Their creation is not controllable from this repo; their deletion is gh-2287's designed sweeper behavior and their naming in the sweep issue is the designed signal to the owner.

**Fix approach** (minimum, mirrors the gh-2230 criterion exactly): teach the daily sweeper the failed-train shape — in `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`, a **fresh** draft carrying a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker is reclaimed immediately (any age) when (a) its owner run has COMPLETED, and (b) the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train is a failure whose `release-provenance` job ("Sign release checksums") is SKIPPED — i.e. the publish point is unreachable, so nobody can ever publish it. Everything else keeps the current semantics: fresh unmarked/human drafts untouched (E1), owner in-flight untouched (mid-upload fail-safe), provenance FAILED (rerunnable `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-1899) untouched until the existing 24h sweep, train-lookup failure keeps (never delete blind). The sweep issue names the reclaimed draft + failed train via the existing gh-2105 diagnosis, and the next clean sweep auto-closes it.

**Previous attempt**: gh-2230 (PR #2232, commit `cdf3467b`) added the train-level `train-draft-guard` job — correct for drafts that exist with a completed owner at train end, but one-shot: it cannot see drafts created after it ran (long daily-child attach legs) and never revisits drafts it kept for in-flight owners. Insufficient for the recurring sweep-issue class by itself; this fix adds the sweep-side re-examination that closes both residual shapes.

train_diagnosis() {
 local tag="$1" train_json failed_train train_id jobs_json
 train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
   --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
   --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")

       end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 [ -n "$failed_train" ] || return 0
 train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 jobs_json=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s' \
   "$train_id" \

# ── failed-train diagnosis (gh-2105 + gh-2318) ──────────────────────────────
# The staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's push run on
# the tag ref — release-provenance is the sole publish point, gh-1801).
# Diagnose <tag>'s newest CONCLUDED failed ci.yml push train; prints one
# TSV row:
#
#   train_id <TAB> conclusion <TAB> url <TAB> failed_jobs <TAB> prov_conclusion
#
# `failed_jobs` names the train's failure-concluded jobs (the gh-2105 issue
# prose). `prov_conclusion` is the release-provenance job's OWN conclusion —
# "skipped" means the publish point is UNREACHABLE (`rerun --failed` never
# resurrects skipped jobs — the gh-2230 train-guard criterion), "failure"
# means it is rerunnable (the staged draft is the `rerun --failed` recovery
# vessel, gh-189 — the stale 24h sweep reclaims it if the train is never
# recovered). The publish-point job is matched by its ci.yml `name:` —
# "Sign release checksums" (pinned by test/release_hygiene_test.dart,
# gh-2318 group; update both together). Empty output = no failed train /
# lookup failed; every consumer degrades fail-safe (keep), and nothing
# here may gate the stale >24h delete (the diagnosis is never a
# precondition — gh-2105).
train_diagnosis() {
  local tag="$1" train_json failed_train train_id jobs_json
  train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
    --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
  failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
    ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
      | if . == null then empty else
          {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
        end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  [ -n "$failed_train" ] || return 0
  train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  jobs_json=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s' \
    "$train_id" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '([.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums")][0].conclusion // "")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
}

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   stale + pipeline (bot author, the machine account, or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { bucket: (
          if ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
# gh-2318: fresh (<24h) pipeline drafts reclaimed early — provably
# never-publishable (completed owner, failed train with skipped
# release-provenance). Tracked separately from the >24h sweep deletions.
reclaimed=""
reclaimed_tags=""
reclaimed_count=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0

  case "$bucket" in
    fresh)

      # own the draft, but a fresh draft can already be PROVABLY
      # never-publishable: the v1.0.739 shape — a daily-child staging leg
      # minted the tag (release_tag_mint.sh) and staged the draft, the
      # freshly fired train failed upstream of release-provenance, and the
      # gh-2230 train-draft-guard either ran before the draft existed (a
      # long attach leg created it later) or kept it while its owner was
      # still in-flight. Nothing re-examined such a draft with train
      # knowledge, so it rotted the full 24h and re-filed the recurring
      # sweep issue. Apply the train guard's EXACT criterion here —
      # reclaim only a well-formed-marker draft whose owner run COMPLETED
      # and whose tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with
      # release-provenance SKIPPED (rerun --failed cannot resurrect
      # skipped jobs — nobody will ever publish it). Fail-safe keeps
      # mirror the train guard: unmarked/human drafts (E1), an in-flight
      # owner run (possibly mid-upload), a rerunnable FAILED provenance
      # (that draft stays the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-189,
      # until the stale sweep), any lookup failure (never delete blind),
      # and untagged drafts (no train to diagnose).

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issue recurs for failed tag trains. v1.0.739's tag was minted at 2026-11-17T05:26:23Z by a daily-child draft-staging leg (`release_tag_mint.sh` → tagger `github-actions[bot]`, same second as the draft's `created_at`; draft author `@IstiN` via RELEASE_PAT, marker run/402346218 — not a ci.yml run), so its train ran the ci.yml at the tag ref — commit `c08bbe26` (01:04Z), which predates the gh-2230 fix (`cdf3467b`, 07:32Z): no `train-draft-guard` existed on that train, the draft rotted 44h and was swept. Post-fix the guard is still one-shot: a dead-train draft created AFTER it ran (long daily-child attach legs: build-mobile ≈3h, build-windows ≈85m) or kept for an in-flight owner at train end is never re-examined with train knowledge — the 24h sweep was the only net, re-filing the recurring issue.

### Previous Attempt

gh-2230 (PR #2232) added the train-level `train-draft-guard` job — correct for drafts visible with a completed owner at train end, but it cannot see drafts born later and never revisits keeps; the failed-train draft class kept recurring.

### Fix

- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: a fresh (<24h) draft is reclaimed immediately when its well-formed `release-draft-owner` marker names a COMPLETED run and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with release-provenance ("Sign release checksums") SKIPPED — the publish point is unreachable, `rerun --failed` cannot resurrect skipped jobs. Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard: unmarked/human drafts (E1), in-flight owner (mid-upload), rerunnable FAILED provenance (gh-189 `rerun --failed` recovery vessel — waits for the 24h sweep), any lookup failure (never delete blind). arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The recurring `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issue: v1.0.739's tag was minted by a daily-child staging leg (tagger `github-actions[bot]`, same second as the draft; marker run/402346218 — not a ci.yml run), so its train ran the PRE-fix ci.yml (tag commit `c08bbe26` predates gh-2230's `cdf3467b` by 6h) — no `train-draft-guard` existed, and the draft rotted 44h. Post-fix the guard is still one-shot: a dead-train draft created after it ran (long attach legs) or kept for an in-flight owner is never re-examined with train knowledge.

### Previous Attempt

gh-2230 (PR #2232) added the train-level guard — correct only for drafts visible with a completed owner at train end; the failed-train draft class kept recurring.

### Fix

- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: reclaim a fresh (<24h) draft immediately when its `release-draft-owner` marker names a COMPLETED run and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml train failed with release-provenance SKIPPED (publish point unreachable — `rerun --failed` can't resurrect skipped jobs). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard: unmarked/human (E1), in-flight owner, FAILED provenance (gh-189 rerun vessel), lookup failure (never delete blind). Shared `train_diagnosis()` helper; issue names the train, auto-closes on clean sweep.
- `docs/ci.md` + CHANGELOG document the reclaim. The 11 `ai-*` machine drafts are created outside this repo's runners (gh-2287 handles them by design).

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` `gh-2318` group (6 tests): twin reclaims (multi-item), in-flight/rerunnable/green-train/undiagnosable keeps, publish-point job-name pin. RED before the fix, GREEN after; full `release_hygiene_test.dart` (75) + `release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart` (27) green.
- `dart test --exclude-tags integration` green; analyze/format clean for touched files.

### Notes

- No workflow changes — `sweep-drafts` already grants `contents: write` + `actions: read`. v1.0.739's content shipped via v1.0.740+ (no publish gap).

#     User-typed and marker-less but machine-created), OR the body
#     carries a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>`
#     marker — the exact shape

#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);

#     unreachable — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs, so
#     nobody will ever publish it; the same criterion as ci.yml's gh-2230
#     train-draft-guard, which only sees drafts visible at train end).
#     A rerunnable (FAILED) provenance keeps the draft as the rerun
#     --failed recovery vessel (gh-189) until it goes stale below;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.

# gh-2287: the ai-teammate factory's drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are User-typed

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  CROSS-MODULE DUPLICATION GATE (issue #487) — ONLY TIGHTEN THE THRESHOLD  ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# The per-package jscpd gates (dup stage: core lib/ < 1%, flutter_app/lib/
# < 3.7%) only see duplication INSIDE one module. Copy-paste ACROSS module
# boundaries (lib, bin ↔ flutter_app/lib ↔ packages/*/lib ↔ browser_ext/dart)
# was invisible — issue #487 measured 20 files shipped as cross-module
# clones (OAuth callback, ASR tool, chrome/persistent web env, fahx import…).

**Full suite: 14,658 passed, 16 skipped (platform-gated), 0 failures.** Everything is verified and final. 

## Summary

**Ticket gh-2318** (`[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept`) — an auto-filed sweep issue whose own text names the real defect: *"recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)"*.

**Root cause** (two layers, both in-repo):
1. **v1.0.739's train predates the gh-2230 guard.** Forensics from the live repo: the tag was minted 05:26:23Z by a daily-child staging leg (tagger `github-actions[bot]` via `release_tag_mint.sh`, same second as the draft's `created_at`; draft author `@IstiN` via RELEASE_PAT, marker `run/402346218` — a build-macos run, not ci.yml). The train therefore executed the ci.yml **at the tag ref** — commit `c08bbe26` (01:04Z), 6h before the fix commit `cdf3467b` (07:32Z) — so no `train-draft-guard` existed; the draft rotted 44h.
2. **The gh-2230 guard is one-shot**, so the class recurs post-fix: a dead-train draft created *after* train end (long attach legs: build-mobile ≈3h) or kept for an in-flight owner is never re-examined with train knowledge — the 24h sweep re-files the issue every time.

**Fix**: `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` now reclaims a fresh (<24h) draft immediately when its `release-draft-owner` marker names a COMPLETED run and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml train failed with release-provenance (`Sign release checksums`) SKIPPED — the exact gh-2230 criterion (publish point unreachable, `rerun --failed` can't resurrect skips). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard (E1 human, in-flight owner, rerunnable FAILED provenance = gh-189 rerun vessel, lookup failures). Shared `train_diagnosis()` helper; the issue names the train and auto-closes on the next clean sweep.

**TDD**: 6 new tests in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (multi-item twin reclaim + 4 keep-path pins + job-name pin) — RED before the fix, GREEN after. Independent sandbox run reproduced the exact v1.0.739 shape end-to-end.

**Not fixable here** (documented, not assumed): the 11 `ai-gh-*`/`ai-pr-*` machine drafts are created by the @ai-teammate automation loop outside this repo's runners; their deletion is gh-2287's designed behavior.

**Committed**: `b81d4c7da3 fix(2318): sweep reclaims fresh never-publishable drafts (dead train, completed owner)` on `ai/gh-2318` (above `origin/main`; no closing keywords). Working tree clean.
